access: visual inspection of rendered relevant pages

source_audit.declaration: The fault author inspected only the frozen PDF among project materials. The destination files in this new author_freeze directory were authored from that PDF alone.

public_contract_basis.assurance_boundary: honest mandatory-event-complete capture with byte-bound records; replay is trace-relative and not an independent live observer

fixed_case_scope.schedule: batch-one sequential round-major calls on one CUDA stream per rank

excluded_unclaimed_capabilities: transient mutation that is fully restored between registered snapshots

common_protocol.pairing: For each fault, rebuild one clean control and one mutant from the same frozen N=2 case identity; apply exactly one named injection only to the mutant.
common_protocol.capture: Keep all applicable gates enabled and require honest, mandatory-event-complete setup, registered-transition, ordered execution, and final records.
common_protocol.selection: Freeze request, phase, layer/call ordinal, and payload before either member of a pair executes. The concrete selection rule is stated per fault.
common_protocol.clean_gate: The matched clean member must have complete mandatory coverage for every applicable target, valid byte binding, passing replay predicates, Python-call-scope dispatch pass with compiled scope still labeled partial, and no operational exception.
common_protocol.mutant_success: The clean gate passes; the exact injection receipt is present; the mutant reaches its expected primary predicate with all earlier unrelated predicates passing; and no missing record or unallowlisted exception substitutes for detection.
common_protocol.mutant_failure: Any clean-gate failure, absent or ambiguous injection, missing mandatory record, earlier unrelated failure, unallowlisted exception, or mutant passage of the expected primary predicate is a failed fault trial.
common_protocol.semantics_policy: Token/logit/logical-KV/GDN results are secondary localization evidence unless a fault explicitly names cross-arm equivalence as its primary port; unchanged semantics do not rescue a failed pre-output contract.

faults.title: Write one append token before the private-tail copy
faults.public_target: tail-safe append, with prefix immutability as a redundant port
faults.realistic_failure_mode: A lazy COW path checks or performs detachment after issuing the first append store, so the shared document tail receives one write before the private page exists.

frozen_injection.cell: shared-document KV with borrowed GDN, N=2
frozen_injection.locus: the first full-attention layer in frozen model order at the registered 32-token transition
frozen_injection.action: Issue exactly the first append write to the still-shared 128-token last document page, then perform the otherwise correct 127-token valid-tail copy and continue normally.

expected_invariants: Exactly one private copy of the 127 valid tail tokens exists for the selected request/layer.
The tail-copy event ordinal is strictly smaller than every append-write ordinal touching its logical destination.
The shared physical document page digest is unchanged from setup through registered transition and final capture.

detection_ports.primary: ordered copied-tail and append receipts: copy_ordinal < first_write_ordinal
detection_ports.redundant: physical document-KV setup digest equals transition/final digest

faults.clean_gate: The selected clean row has one role-correct private-tail copy before every append write and an unchanged shared-page digest.
faults.success_criterion: The mutant has an honest first-write ordinal less than or equal to the copy ordinal, while all earlier identity/storage-role checks pass.
faults.failure_criterion: The clean row fails; the mutant omits COW instead of delaying it; the shared page was already private; the required ordering records are missing; or the ordering predicate passes.
faults.why_fresh: Unlike the PDF's omitted-COW fault, a private copy is eventually made and the mutation isolates ordering rather than copy existence.

faults.title: Corrupt only the unused lane of the shared partial document page
faults.realistic_failure_mode: A page initializer or scrubber overruns its intended private allocation by one token lane and writes into the inactive lane of the shared document's 127-of-128 tail page.

frozen_injection.cell: shared-document KV with materialized GDN, N=2
frozen_injection.locus: after setup capture and before any private-tail copy at the first full-attention layer in frozen model order
frozen_injection.action: Flip the lowest bit of the first byte in the one inactive token lane of that layer's shared K page only; do not alter any valid document token or any V bytes.

expected_invariants: The physical document page, including inactive/padding bytes bound by its archived artifact, has identical setup, transition, and final digests.
Logical valid-token KV may remain unchanged, but physical prefix immutability is not limited to currently read tokens.

detection_ports.primary: physical document-K digest equality across setup, registered transition, and final
detection_ports.secondary: byte-bound artifact digest/manifest consistency for the captured mutated page

faults.clean_gate: All physical document K/V page digests, including the partial page backing bytes, remain identical across phases.
faults.success_criterion: Only the selected inactive lane differs and the prefix-immutability replay rejects the mutant; valid logical KV and semantics may remain identical.
faults.failure_criterion: The clean row changes; a valid token is modified; the mutation lands in a private page; capture excludes the mutated backing bytes; or the physical prefix digest remains equal.
faults.why_fresh: This is neither missing COW nor request aliasing; it tests whole-physical-prefix immutability against a one-lane bounds error that can be semantically silent.

faults.title: Commit one model call twice while discarding the first result
faults.realistic_failure_mode: A retry path treats a completed call as failed and reissues it without rolling back KV/GDN state, causing an extra committed state transition even though only one result is surfaced.

frozen_injection.cell: shared-document KV with borrowed GDN, N=2
frozen_injection.locus: the first generated-token feedback call after the registered query transition
frozen_injection.action: Execute and commit the frozen call once, discard only its returned output, then execute the same request/input call again before r1's call; retain both honest call and append receipts.
do_not_change: positions presented by the retry path

expected_invariants: The ordered call ledger has exactly the cardinality and request-round order fixed by the sequential round-major schedule.
Each scheduled state-appended input has exactly one committed append/call transition.
Discarding an output does not erase a committed call from the mandatory execution record.

detection_ports.primary: frozen ordered-call cardinality and request/round ordinal replay
detection_ports.redundant: ordered append history and final logical-KV/GDN cross-arm equivalence

faults.clean_gate: The clean ledger contains exactly one call for every frozen request-round slot and exactly 39 state-appended inputs per completed request.
faults.success_criterion: The mutant contains one extra honest committed call receipt at the frozen locus and fails schedule/cardinality replay before any semantic comparison is used as rescue.
faults.failure_criterion: The clean schedule fails; the first call is rolled back or never committed; the extra call is omitted from capture; an unrelated exception occurs first; or exact schedule/cardinality replay passes.
faults.why_fresh: This duplicates a correctly bound request call; it does not swap sequence identities, alter positions, change a mask, or replace the callable.

faults.title: Use a doubled effective attention scale for one otherwise valid call
faults.realistic_failure_mode: A refactor or configuration cache supplies the effective scale for a different head geometry while preserving the same callable and all other call arguments.

frozen_injection.cell: shared-document KV with materialized GDN, N=2
frozen_injection.locus: the first full-attention call in frozen model order at the registered 32-token transition
frozen_injection.action: Pass effective_scale = 2 * frozen_effective_scale for this call only.

expected_invariants: Every ordered attention call receipt binds the effective scale fixed by identity/protocol for that call geometry.
The two ownership controls use equal effective scale for the same query and schedule.

detection_ports.primary: ordered call receipt effective_scale equals the frozen protocol value bit-for-bit in its declared scalar encoding
detection_ports.secondary: cross-arm canonical full-logit/logical-KV/GDN equivalence; a selected numerical sidecar may corroborate but is not required

faults.clean_gate: The matched clean call receipt carries the frozen scale and the Python-call-scope dispatch replay passes.
faults.success_criterion: The mutant receipt truthfully carries exactly twice the frozen scale and the scale-contract predicate rejects it with earlier identity/callable/query/mask/position/view checks passing.
faults.failure_criterion: The clean row fails; scale is not independently recorded; another call argument changes; an unrelated gate fires first; or the frozen-scale equality predicate passes.
faults.why_fresh: The PDF faults alter position, mask, callable, or view; none alters only the recorded effective scale that the public contract explicitly binds.

faults.title: Allocate correct private GDN tensors but retain the borrowed-base binding token
faults.realistic_failure_mode: Physical copy/rebind succeeds, but lifecycle metadata update is lost, leaving a completed request with the pretransition binding token even though its storage token/ranges changed.

frozen_injection.cell: shared-document KV with borrowed GDN, N=2
frozen_injection.locus: immediately after the registered 32-token transition has produced all 60 request-private GDN tensors
frozen_injection.action: Keep all 60 private tensor objects and contents unchanged, but retain r1's setup-phase binding token as its transition binding token; preserve the new physical storage token and honest range records.

expected_invariants: A completed borrowed request changes both binding and storage tokens at transition.
All 60 completed-request ranges are disjoint from base and peer ranges.
The lifecycle request ID is stable while its phase binding token advances exactly once for the rebind.

detection_ports.redundant: transition storage token differs from setup and all 60 normalized ranges are private, demonstrating the metadata/storage contradiction

faults.clean_gate: For both completed requests, binding and storage tokens change at transition and all 60 tensor ranges are disjoint from base and peers.
faults.success_criterion: The mutant's physical ownership predicates pass, but lifecycle replay rejects the unchanged binding token for r1 at the registered transition.
faults.failure_criterion: The clean row fails; any GDN range aliases base/peer; tensor contents change; the binding token is not a mandatory captured field; an unrelated gate fires first; or the token-change predicate passes.
faults.why_fresh: The PDF's GDN faults create physical base/peer aliases; this fault preserves correct disjoint storage and isolates stale rebind metadata explicitly required by the public pointer-free schema.
